correctness.rationale: Scalar parts of square-zero elements vanish. Squaring a+b+c in the augmentation ideal gives 2a∧b; top degree is radical. Projection to U in degree one forces the pure degree-two part to be U^perp by polarization and maximality. Its dimension 3-r, and the perfect pairing then gives exactly one maximal space for each alternating form on U with values in the top-degree line. Mixed cubic products cancel; hence W²=∧²U and closure is equivalent to ∧³U=0. The characteristic filtration preserves r, while GL(V) moves U and conjugation by 1+a adds the restrictions of -2a∧u∧v; these exhaust the form parameters. For an intersection of two quotient spaces the pure degree-two kernel is (U+U')^perp; its projected image is the radical of the difference of forms restricted to U∩U'. This gives all stated dimensions and the point/hyperplane equations using a common volume identification. Witt extension gives uniform incidence for the nonzero isotropic vectors; dividing the count of space–vector incidences gives 2(q+1). Independent bitmask multiplication over F_3 exhausted 33,880 candidate quotient 3-spaces, found all 80 with the stated product ranks and intersection totals, and checked 780 noncentral square-zero elements, each in eight spaces. The symbolic proof covers the general field, not extrapolation from this test.
residual_risks: No claim about characteristic two, larger exterior rank, or maximality among subalgebras under a different inclusion order.
